discoveries.title: Cycle-time overrun: the runner's 20-minute child ceiling against a cycle over the real backlog
evidence: scripts/pilot-runner.mts runOneCycle timeout: 20 * 60_000
docs/evidence/autonomy-recovery-cycle-post-fix-2026-09-01.txt (start and EXIT timestamps)
discoveries.measured: 17m00s for one --max=100 cycle over the real backlog (03:26:56Z to 03:43:56Z, exit 0): about 10 min opening/resuming 100 occurrences serially against Neon, about 7 min dispatching. Three minutes short of the runner's 20-minute kill, on latency alone.
discoveries.fix: The shared cycle now takes an injected dispatch budget (runCycle.budget); freshness-shadow passes --budget-min (default 15, from process start) and pilot-runner passes it through, so a cycle stops STARTING work at 15 minutes, defers the rest by name, writes its record and exits clean inside the 20-minute backstop. tests/cycle-budget.test.ts pins it with a moved clock.
discoveries.live_proof: pnpm pilot:run --cycles=1 --max=5 --budget-min=3 through the real runner path (digest to a scratch mirror): the fixed pre-dispatch overhead (~9 min of serial Neon work) exceeded the deliberately tiny 3-minute budget, and the cycle ended CLEAN — exit 0, run record data/health/freshness-shadow-runs/2026-09-01-10.json (dueCount 2858, dispatched 0, deferred 2883, occurrencesOpened 5, preOpenSkipped [], crashed absent), digest delivered, no kill. The same overhead measured against the runner's 20-minute ceiling is why the budget defaults to 15.
discoveries.why_this_class: A timeout-kill mid-dispatch leaks open occurrences and repeats. Measured at 17 of 20 minutes it had not fired yet; it was one slow Neon evening from firing, which is why it is fixed by construction rather than by raising the ceiling.

discoveries.title: Occurrence leak divergence: 393 of 1,447 occurrences had a RouteTask with a committed disposition while only 55 occurrences were closed with one
evidence: docs/evidence/autonomy-recovery-readback-before-2026-09-01.txt
docs/evidence/autonomy-recovery-colliding-row-readback-2026-09-01.txt
discoveries.note: The mechanism, read back from the durable store on the exact row that killed the pre-fix cycle: its RouteTask was already DISPOSED (INGESTED at 19:36Z by the attempt that recorded the artifact), but its occurrence was never closed, so every later cycle RESUMED it — resumeOpenOccurrence checks only occurrence.closedAt, not the RouteTask's disposition — re-claimed the settled task, re-walked, re-recorded, and died: seven Attempts with outcome null, one per dead cycle from 20:56Z to 03:09Z. The post-fix cycle's attempt on the same row closed ABORTED (the second disposition was refused by the domain, caught, abandoned) and the occurrence then closed, with still exactly ONE artifact record. Those seven orphan Attempts also explain the '15 refused' in every reclaim sweep: their leases expire, but reclaim refuses to reopen a settled route. Two efficiencies, not recovery requirements: close an already-disposed occurrence from its RouteTask's existing disposition WITHOUT re-walking, and let the sweep close orphan Attempts on a DISPOSED task as LEASE_EXPIRED without reopening the task.
